Papers in pharmacometrics (PMX) to read, grouped by topic, each with a line on
what it covers.

## T-Cell Engagers

- Chevalier, Zhang, Tolsma and Zager (2026).
  [Synapse-based bispecific immune cell engager model predicts invariance in synapse behavior across different effector-to-tumor cell ratios](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.24.733437v1).
  bioRxiv preprint, posted 29 June 2026, from Pfizer. An ordinary
  differential equation model of trimer formation (CD3, bispecific antibody
  and tumor antigen) within single synapses of one T cell and one target
  cell, with binding in two dimensions. For a given free drug concentration,
  the number of trimers per synapse does not change with the
  effector-to-target (E:T) ratio, which well-mixed models such as the Betts
  trimer model do not capture. The synapse model is then coupled to a tumor
  growth inhibition model, with a threshold of trimers per synapse for
  killing.
- Irby, Hibma, Elmeliegy, Wang, Vandendries, Poels, Shtylla and Williams
  (2025).
  [A novel two-part mixture model for the incidence and time course of cytokine release syndrome after elranatamab dosing in multiple myeloma patients](https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.3533).
  *Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics* 117:1687–1695. Elranatamab is a
  bispecific antibody against CD3 and B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA). The
  first part of the model links the maximum concentration at the time of the first cytokine release syndrome
  (CRS) event to the probability of having CRS at all. The second part is a
  two-state Markov model (CRS or no CRS) for its time course, in which higher
  exposure on day 1 raises the probability of CRS and premedication with
  corticosteroids or IL-6 pathway inhibitors lowers it. The model explains the
  differences between priming regimens.
- Li, Tredennick, Polhamus and others (2026).
  [Epcoritamab step-up dosing regimen selection and optimization using repeated time-to-event modeling for cytokine release syndrome risk mitigation](https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70362).
  *Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics* 120:542–551. Epcoritamab is a
  CD3 × CD20 bispecific antibody. Repeated time-to-event models of Grade ≥2
  CRS, fitted to 600 patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma from EPCORE NHL-1 and
  NHL-3. Prior CAR T-cell therapy lowers the maximum effect of epcoritamab on
  the CRS hazard, and intravenous fluids and dexamethasone in cycle 1 raise
  the concentration needed for half that effect. Simulations support the
  approved two step-up doses for large B-cell lymphoma and three for
  follicular lymphoma. This site's
  [TCE CRS tolerance](../projects/tce-crs-tolerance/index.qmd) project starts
  from this model.
